Subject: Request to add DataSync Labs as subprocessor (Order Form amendment + DPA annex)

Hi Rafael —

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, CloudBridge is onboarding DataSync Labs (datasynclabs.com) to handle encrypted log transformation for our managed connectors. They will process logs and minimally processed telemetry for connector health; they will not retain customer payloads beyond 30 days.

Attached is a short Order Form amendment that adds DataSync as a permitted subprocessor (Proposed_OrderForm_Amendment_vCLB.pdf) plus our proposed DPA annex language redline. Can you confirm whether Redwood can:

- Accept DataSync as a downstream processor under the existing MSA + Order Form?
- Agree to the 30-day retention carveout for this integration?
- Execute a DPA annex (we can push via DocuSign) or do you need our legal to do a countersign?

We'd like to finalize this by end of next week to keep the connector rollout on schedule.

Thanks — please loop in whoever on your side needs to approve the flow-down (legal/procurement/ops).

—Anna

Anna —

Appreciate the note and the attachments. Looping in Kimberly from Legal and Connor from Ops so they can confirm scope and DPA requirements. A few initial items from my side:

- High level: Redwood's standard approach is to accept downstream subprocessors if there is a signed flow-down DPA and the scope is limited.
- We need written confirmation that DataSync will only process telemetry/connector health data, not customer content/payloads. Can you confirm that in writing?
- Retention: 30 days sounds okay in principle, but Legal may ask for a shorter default for certain customers in the EU — Kimberly will advise.

Proposed next step: Kimberly, can you take the redline and indicate whether the DPA annex is acceptable or whether we should propose tweaks (particularly sections on purpose limitation, access controls, and audit rights)? Connor — please confirm ops acceptance for a downstream service that holds KV-style logs for up to 30 days.

If Legal is good, I can route the DocuSign envelope for execution and share the HubSpot deal/DocuSign links with CloudBridge.

Thanks — Rafael

Subject: Re: Request to add DataSync Labs as subprocessor (Order Form amendment + DPA annex)

Folks —

Thanks for the heads-up. I reviewed the redline (DPA_Annex_redline.docx). High level comments:

1) Scope limitation: we need explicit language that DataSync processes "operational telemetry and connector health metrics" only. Any troubleshooting that pulls customer content must be strictly on a per-ticket, timebound basis and require documented authorization.

2) Retention: propose 14 days as our standard for telemetry unless customer-specific jurisdictional requirements demand otherwise. If CloudBridge needs 30 days for engineering reasons, we can accept 30 days for US accounts but require a 14-day default for EU-resident accounts. Please flag whether CloudBridge can support region-specific retention.

3) Security controls: add SOC2 Type II evidence (or equivalent) and a commitment to provide an SSAE/AICPA letter within 30 days of request. Also require MFA for admin access and least-privilege IAM for the service accounts used by DataSync.

4) Subprocessor flow-down: we need a signed flow-down DPA from CloudBridge to DataSync that mirrors our obligations (liability cap carveouts are okay to discuss but not for security obligations).

5) Audit / incident: include a 72-hour notification requirement for any confirmed data incident affecting the telemetry dataset.

I attached a marked-up version with redlines and inline comments (DPA_Annex_redline.docx). Connor — can you confirm whether the telemetry retention/operational constraints are acceptable from an ops perspective (esp. bulk downloads / access provisioning)?

If CloudBridge confirms the scope language and either accepts the US-30 / EU-14 day split or proposes an operational justification, Legal can sign off and we can proceed to DocuSign.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Request to add DataSync Labs as subprocessor (Order Form amendment + DPA annex)

Anna / legal team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per Kimberly's note above, Redwood can provisionally accept DataSync as a permitted subprocessor provided the following are completed and executed:

1) CloudBridge confirms in writing that DataSync will be limited to operational telemetry/connector health and will not process customer content except as explicitly authorized for troubleshooting (ticketed, timebound).
2) Execution of the DPA annex with the agreed retention approach (US accounts = 30 days; EU accounts = 14 days by default) or a CloudBridge-provided justification for broader retention for specific customers.
3) DataSync provides SOC2 Type II evidence (or equivalent) and confirms MFA + least-privilege access controls for the log processing environment.

If you can sign the DPA annex with those points and return via DocuSign, we'll approve the Order Form amendment and publish DataSync into the approved subprocessor inventory. For convenience I created a DocuSign envelope that CloudBridge can use: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/1234abcd — please let us know if you prefer to send the envelope from your side.

Target timeline: return signed DPA + evidence by EOD Friday 6/20 to keep the integration schedule. If any of these items need more time, flag them and we will treat this as a short review path (Rafael/procurement escalation) rather than a full legal escalation.

Best — Rafael

Rafael Mendes
